coverage.category: 18. Transport operators
coverage.found: Strong 2026 trigger in N'Djamena: mototaxi, taxi and minibus drivers need a Transport ministry agrement, a municipal ID number, a yellow vest, a professional card and painted vehicle colours. A 60-day deadline from 9 Apr 2026 has passed, and mixed-force checks are announced. A joint order of the Public Security and Transport ministers sets the conditions. See C01, C02.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: CEMAC Regulation 02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM (2018) and BEAC Instruction 011/GR/2019 require SA or SARL with 50M FCFA capital and licensing. No Chad-specific reporting tool found. See C11 (weak).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections
coverage.found: Private schools: moratorium on new private schools lifted 4 Nov 2025; in 2023 only 669 of 1,025 private schools were compliant; circular of 10 Jul 2026 requires diploma-holding teachers, CDI contracts and at least SMIG pay, with checks at the school-year start. Private health-training schools also told to regularise (circular 9 Sept 2025). Driving schools, tattoo studios and nurseries: nothing found. See C04, C05.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Regulator is ARSAT (downstream hydrocarbons). Feb 2026 note caps jerrycan sales at 60 L per day without ARSAT authorisation; butane shortages and extra import authorisations in late 2025. No licence-renewal or reporting workflow found. See C12 (unverified).

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Gum arabic and sesame exports need a special Ministry of Commerce authorisation (more than 10 documents, per an AfCFTA trade-barrier complaint resolved 6 Feb 2025). Export duty of 5% plus 2% statistical fee since arrete 6 Aug 2025. Nothing new beyond K03.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Microfinance is supervised by COBAC/BEAC (regional). No Chad-specific lists or reporting forms found. Mobile-money payment-institution licences were granted in 2025 (Konoom, Moov Money). Unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers
coverage.found: No clinic-licensing or insurer-billing rule found. Pharmacy side is in category 25.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals
coverage.found: 17 Feb 2025: inspection mission of private pharmaceutical establishments in N'Djamena. 10 Sept 2025: two circulars, one on wholesalers respecting public prices (printed on invoices and boxes, with closure or licence revocation as sanctions), one on storage norms. See C03b below, listed as C13.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security guards unprotected by social security (tchadinfos 2025/09/29); CNPS and labour inspectors can sanction. Labour Code is law 6/PR/2015. No agency licensing found. See C09.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: Only mining items: prospecting suspension (Sept 2026), SONEMIC window. Nothing on construction site registers or local-content reports.

coverage.found: Search found no Chad rules on guest registers or tourist levy. Unverified.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Chadian licensing or register rule for scrap dealers found (one search plus one follow-up). Only context: 2024 press on cable theft at the Kome oil site, with receivers in N'Djamena blamed by the Logone Oriental governor (tchadinfos 2024/08/23 and 2024/10/02). Code de l'environnement art. 57 only promises implementing texts on waste collection, transport and recovery. No dealer register found.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: One search; no Chadian rule on second-hand dealer registers or pawnbrokers found. Results were French, Swiss and Canadian only. Nothing new beyond the absence of a rule.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or used-parts regime found. Related one-offs found: 27 Mar 2025 Public Security circular on fake or missing plates (deadline 24 Apr 2025); June 2025 document-check operation in N'Djamena with a 45-day deadline (carte grise, fiche technique, insurance, customs-clearance proof); Feb 2026 Abeche mairie call for owners of non-cleared vehicles to pay duties at a promotional rate via a joint commission. These are owner-side, state-run, one-off campaigns.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No Chadian beekeeper register, export certification or mandatory report found. Only donor project activity (Swiss PFNL project, 37 beekeepers, Apr 2025). Honey is absent from the 2026-2031 Integrated Framework export priorities (sesame and shea). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Most productive category. Code de l'Eau (loi 016/PR/99) title IX sets an agrement regime for hydraulic works firms. STE said in Feb 2023 that arts. 38 and 47 bar new private commercial or industrial boreholes and gave bakeries, car washes, bottlers, hotels, guesthouses, bars and restaurants 8 days to regularise. Arrete 018/PR/PM/MEE/SG/FNE/2026 sets raw-water abstraction fees, collected and controlled by the Fonds national de l'Eau (FNE); an awareness workshop on declaration and payment duties was held 5 Aug 2026. Arrete text, rates, thresholds and any online portal were not found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No haulier licensing or reporting regime found. N'Djamena sludge emptying is mostly informal and illegal dumping is common (tchadinfos 2026/08/23). Waste pre-collection is a municipal-arrondissement duty, largely informal (about 100-200 FCFA per bag, 2026 report). Old arrete 107/M/SG/95 on household waste. No recurring filing by small operators found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Chadian periodic inspection regime for lifts, boilers or pressure equipment found; results were Canadian, Belgian and French. Periodic vehicle technical inspection is also unconfirmed (only document checks and a mention of a 'controle technique' commission communique, undated). Unverified, likely nothing.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: State is owner of water works. In semi-urban centres the Direction de l'Hydraulique or local authorities delegate management to user associations (AUE) and, recently, small private operators. Rural water points are run by village committees. STE holds the concession in 11 centres. No filing or reporting duty on small operators found; cost recovery and management are donor-project driven (SEVES/AGIR pilots). Related to the Fonds national de l'Eau fee, see the ledger.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No Chadian funeral-business licensing or cemetery register rule found; results were French and Swiss. Only context: state morgues saturated (CHU de N'Djamena, 52 lockers, 84 bodies) and a 2024 family dispute over a body. Nothing actionable.

result.competitor: Not found. Searches found no digital enrolment app or platform for N'Djamena. Enrolment is done in person at the Voirie urbaine. Similar tools exist only elsewhere (a Yaounde IV moto app, Douala enrolment). The checks to pass are physical (vest, card, paint, number). The national moto-taxi union (SNMT) and the municipal committee are the natural intermediaries and run their own campaign to get drivers to sign up.
result.duty: Real and current, but mostly a one-time registration in person rather than a recurring software workflow. The Commune of N'Djamena issued a note on 9 Apr 2026 that gave mototaxi, taxi and minibus operators 60 days (until about early June 2026) to comply. The requirements are a Transport Ministry agrement, enrolment and an ID number at the Voirie urbaine, vehicle colours and visible numbers, and a helmet. The legal basis is a joint order (arrete conjoint) of the Public Security and Transport ministries. Its number and date are not published in the sources found, so it is unverified. After the deadline, mixed security forces are to run checks, with sanctions "conformement aux textes en vigueur", but no amounts are given. Alwihda (June 2026) says the agrement cost is halved for 2026 for moto-taxis. It also mentions a professional card issued by the city, a vest sold at a promotional price and a portique number for taxis and minibuses. Helmets are not required in the initial phase. Annual renewal is not stated anywhere: the reduced fees apply to "2026", which hints at a yearly fee but does not confirm one. No report of enforcement after June was found. An Aug 2026 article says moto-taxis seem to be sidestepping the authorities' decisions.
result.market: Not reached. No register or statistic giving the number of moto-taxi, taxi or minibus drivers in N'Djamena was found. It is plausibly in the tens of thousands of informal "clandomen", but this is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real (municipal note of 9 Apr 2026 plus the joint ministerial order), and no digital tool exists. But it is mainly a one-time enrolment in person at the Voirie urbaine. The proof drivers must show is physical (vest, professional card, paint, number), so a "compliance wallet" adds little value. Renewal frequency is unconfirmed, and enforcement appears weak: no reports of checks after June, and an August article notes drivers ignoring the rules. Buyers are low-income informal drivers who are unlikely to pay. The only channels are the SNMT union and the city committee, which run the process themselves. Market size is unverified. A solo founder would have few ways to make money beyond a facilitation service for agrement paperwork.

result.competitor: None found. Searches (French: FNE redevance forage déclaration paiement; recouvrement redevance eau brute 2026) found no software, app, online FNE portal or done-for-you service. The regime appears to be at an early awareness stage, so the lack of tools reflects immaturity rather than an unmet need.
result.duty: Partly confirmed. Arrêté n°018/PR/PM/MEE/SG/FNE/2026 on raw-water abstraction fees under the Code de l'Eau (loi 016/PR/99) exists, and the FNE controls and collects the fee. A MEE/UNICEF workshop on 5 Aug 2026 covered declaration and payment duties. The arrêté text was not found, so the following are unverifiable: rates, which users are in scope, volume thresholds, declaration frequency, penalties, payment channel and in-force date. A Code de l'Eau application-tracking document lists the art. 47 decree on private-borehole fee rates as 'to be drafted'. In Feb 2023 STE gave commercial borehole users (bakeries, car washes, bottlers, hotels, bars, restaurants) 8 days to comply. It cited arts. 38 and 47, which give STE exclusivity and ban new commercial private boreholes in served areas. The penalty was unspecified: 'legal channels'. This exposes users to illegality if they declare.
result.market: Not reached. No register or statistic of private commercial borehole users in Chad was found. The market is plausibly a few hundred to low thousands of firms, mostly in N'Djamena. That is a small national market, and many of those users may operate boreholes illegally under art. 47.
result.reason: The arrêté (n°018/PR/PM/MEE/SG/FNE/2026) exists and the FNE controls and collects the fee. No source found gives rates, who pays, filing frequency, penalties, payment channel or whether collection has started. As of August 2026 it was still at the awareness-workshop stage. There is also a legal conflict. STE says Code de l'Eau arts. 38 and 47 make it the exclusive potable-water provider and ban new commercial boreholes in its service area. Many target buyers may therefore be unlawful users who avoid declaring. No software or state portal was found, but that reflects how immature the regime is rather than unmet demand. The market is small and willingness to pay is low. The likely obligation is a simple periodic payment that doesn't need software.

Duty is real: ministry circulars of 10 Sept 2025 require public prices on supply invoices and boxes, plus storage norms. Sanctions run from temporary closure to licence revocation. A Nov 2025 article gave pharmacists three months to comply. These are one-off administrative circulars, not a recurring filing with a portal or fixed frequency. I found no software or state price database doing the job, but searches were thin. The market is tiny and mostly informal: 2020 figures of 52 officines, 381 depots and 36 wholesalers (a journal citation, not the original register). Low willingness to pay and weak recurrence. Price labelling is a compliance step, not a workflow. Score 3.

The duty is real but weak as a software market. The 10 Jul 2026 circular (tchadinfos) requires state-recognised diplomas, CDI contracts and pay at least SMIG. It sets no deadline and names no penalty ("toute violation sera sanctionnée"); checks are announced for the next school year start. The 2023 article reports 1,025 private schools, of which 669 were regulatory. I found no state platform or compliance software, but only two searches were run, so that is not exhaustive. Frequency is low: there is no recurring filing. Schools are small, informal and unlikely to pay. I did not open the Nov 2025 arrete article. The authorisation checklist and fees were not checked.

Search results (summaries, not opened pages) say Chad suspended new prospecting authorisations on 11 Sept 2026 and that a 21 Sept 2026 note took the gold one-stop window away from SONEMIC and gave it to the Mines Ministry after a 15 Sept decree. So the trigger is shaky and the state is centralising the process. The duty is real but is one-off permit applications, not a recurring workflow. Buyers are mostly informal and security is poor. No competing software found, but no recurring filing or register of buyers found either. Official decree text and buyer counts were not reached. Only 2 searches were run.
